svg.title: AI Academy Level 3 motif sprite sheet
svg.desc: A hidden library of reusable motif symbols for Level 3 figures: slopes and descent, tensors and shapes, neurons and networks, model evaluation, convolution, clustering and text.

symbol.title: The slope at one point on a curve
symbol.desc: A curve rising to the right. At the point where w is 3 and the loss is 9, a straight line just touches the curve. A small step of plus 0.5 across and plus 3.0 up is marked on that line, and a callout says 3.0 divided by 0.5 gives a slope of 6.

symbol.title: Four steps down the loss bowl
symbol.desc: A bowl-shaped curve. Four numbered points walk down the right-hand wall towards the bottom, each one labelled with its own w and loss: 3.00 and 9.00, then 2.40 and 5.76, then 1.92 and 3.69, then 1.54 and 2.36. The bottom of the bowl is marked as the place where the slope is zero.
symbol.text: the bottom: slope 0, nowhere left to go

symbol.title: A learning rate that is too small
symbol.desc: The same bowl-shaped curve. Four dots sit almost on top of each other high on the right-hand wall, joined by arrows so short they are hard to see. The caption reads lr = 0.01, barely moves.

symbol.title: A learning rate that works
symbol.desc: The same bowl-shaped curve. Five dots step steadily down the right-hand wall towards the bottom, each step a little shorter than the last. The caption reads lr = 0.1, walks down.

symbol.title: A learning rate that diverges
symbol.desc: The same bowl-shaped curve. A dot high on the right wall leaps across the bowl to the far wall, then leaps back even higher, each jump landing further up than the last. The caption reads lr = 1.1, leaps and climbs.

symbol.title: A 1-D tensor is one row of numbers
symbol.desc: A single wide bar divided into five equal cells, with a mono label reading shape open bracket 5 comma close bracket pinned to its top-right corner, and a bracket underneath labelled 5 numbers.
symbol.text: one row: 5 features for one delivery

symbol.title: A 2-D tensor is rows and columns
symbol.desc: A block divided into three rows and four columns, with a mono label reading shape 3 comma 4 pinned to its top-right corner. The left edge is labelled 3 rows and the bottom edge 4 columns.
symbol.text: rows are examples · columns are features

symbol.title: A 3-D tensor is a stack of tables
symbol.desc: A shallow three-dimensional box drawn with a front face, a top face and a right face. A mono label reads shape 3 comma 32 comma 32. The depth is labelled 3 channels, the width 32 wide and the height 32 high.
symbol.text: one colour image: 3 channels of 32 by 32

symbol.title: A 4-D tensor is a batch of 3-D tensors
symbol.desc: Three shallow three-dimensional boxes stacked one behind the other going up and to the right. A mono label reads shape 64 comma 3 comma 32 comma 32, the depth of the stack is labelled 64 images, and a note says the first number is always the batch size.
symbol.text: the first number is always the batch size

symbol.title: A matrix multiply cancels the inner numbers
symbol.desc: Two blocks side by side with a multiplication sign between them and an equals sign after. The first is labelled 750 by 2, the second 2 by 16, and the two 2s are boxed in pink and joined to a callout reading the inner numbers must match. The answer block is labelled 750 by 16.
symbol.text: the two 2s must match, and then they vanish
what is left is (750, 16): X's rows, W1's columns

symbol.title: A shape mismatch, and where to look
symbol.desc: The same two blocks with a multiplication sign, but the second is labelled 16 by 2. The inner numbers, 2 and 16, are boxed in red and joined to a callout reading 2 and 16 do not match. Where the answer should be there is a red box with a cross in it and the words no result.
symbol.text: a shape error is a wiring error, not a maths error
the fix: build W1 as (2, 16), or transpose it
print every shape before you multiply

symbol.title: One neuron: multiply, add, squash
symbol.desc: Two input circles holding 1.0 and 2.0 feed into a circle labelled sum, along wires labelled times 0.5 and times 0.8. A third wire brings in a bias of 0.1. The sum, 2.20, passes into a box labelled ReLU and out to an output circle holding 2.20. Underneath, the whole calculation is written out as 1.0 times 0.5 plus 2.0 times 0.8 plus 0.1 equals 2.20.

symbol.title: A network with the shapes written between the layers
symbol.desc: Two input circles on the left connect to five hidden circles in the middle, which connect to one output circle on the right. Above the wires, mono labels read W1 2 by 16 and W2 16 by 1. Below each column, mono labels read 750 by 2, then 750 by 16, then 750 by 1.
symbol.text: the batch size 750 never changes; the last number does

symbol.title: Forward and backward over the same wires
symbol.desc: A small network with two inputs, four hidden units and one output. A solid blue arrow runs left to right above it, labelled forward, numbers flow right, ending at the word output. A dashed pink arrow runs right to left below it, labelled backward, blame flows left, ending at the word blame.
symbol.text: the same weights, used twice: forwards, then backwards

symbol.title: The confusion matrix: all four numbers named
symbol.desc: A two by two table. Rows are what actually happened, columns are what the model said. Top left, True Negative, 75, with a tick. Top right, False Positive, 5, with a cross. Bottom left, False Negative, 4, with a cross. Bottom right, True Positive, 16, with a tick.
symbol.text: one accuracy number hides three of these

symbol.title: Precision reads down the predicted-spam column
symbol.desc: The same two by two table of 75, 5, 4 and 16. A pink outline surrounds the whole predicted-spam column, whose header now reads predicted spam, 21. Underneath: of the 21 I flagged, 16 were spam, and 16 divided by 21 equals 0.7619.
symbol.text: precision: of the 21 I flagged, 16 were spam

symbol.title: Recall reads across the actual-spam row
symbol.desc: The same two by two table of 75, 5, 4 and 16. A pink outline surrounds the whole actual-spam row, whose label now reads actual spam, 20. Underneath: of the 20 real spam, I caught 16, and 16 divided by 20 equals 0.8000.
symbol.text: recall: of the 20 real spam, I caught 16

symbol.title: One ROC curve, three thresholds marked
symbol.desc: A staircase curve climbing from the bottom-left corner to the top-right of a square, well above the dashed diagonal marked chance. Three points on it are ringed and numbered 1, 2 and 3, labelled t = 0.90, t = 0.50 and t = 0.20. The axes are false positive rate and true positive rate.

symbol.title: One split, three piles, three jobs
symbol.desc: A single wide bar cut into three: a large train segment holding 1200, then a validation segment holding 400, then a test segment holding 400, labelled 60 percent, 20 percent and 20 percent. Below, three colour-keyed lines give each pile its one job.
symbol.text: train — fit the model on this
validation — choose options, again and again
test — open once, at the very end

symbol.title: The leaking pipeline: scale first, split second
symbol.desc: A column of three boxes. All 2000 rows flow into a red box reading fit the scaler on all 2000 rows, and split afterwards, which then flows into a train pile of 1600 and a test pile of 400. The note underneath reads the mean has already seen the test rows.
symbol.text: the mean has already seen the test rows

symbol.title: The clean pipeline: split first, fit second
symbol.desc: The same column of three boxes. All 2000 rows flow into a green box reading split first, then fit the scaler on the train rows only, which then flows into a train pile of 1600 and a test pile of 400. The note underneath reads the test rows never touched the mean.
symbol.text: split first, then fit the scaler
the test rows never touched the mean

symbol.title: One cell of a feature map, worked out in full
symbol.desc: A six by six grid of pixels, bright 10s on the left and dark 2s on the right, with a pink outline round the top-left three by three window. A multiplication sign, then the three by three kernel of 1, 0 and minus 1. An arrow points to a four by four feature map whose second cell, outlined in pink, holds 24. A callout shows one row giving 1 times 10 plus 0 times 10 plus minus 1 times 2 equals 8, and three rows giving 8 plus 8 plus 8 equals 24.
symbol.text: three rows: 8 + 8 + 8 = 24, so this output cell is 24

symbol.title: A feature-map stack is one map per filter
symbol.desc: Four square maps drawn one behind the other, going up and to the right, so they read as a shallow three-dimensional block. The depth is labelled 32 channels, a mono label reads shape 32 comma 32 comma 32, and a note says each map is 32 by 32.
symbol.text: a feature-map stack: one map per filter

symbol.title: k-means, the start: two centroids in one blob
symbol.desc: Six hollow points, three bunched at the bottom left and three at the top right. Two ringed cross-hair centroid markers both sit inside the bottom-left bunch, one of them right on top of a point. The caption reads Start, both centroids sit left.

symbol.title: k-means, after one round: one point in the wrong cluster
symbol.desc: The same six points. Two at the bottom left are now filled circles; the other four, including the third bottom-left point, are triangles. The two centroid markers have moved apart. The caption reads After iteration 1, 2 and 4, C went right.

symbol.title: k-means, settled: three and three
symbol.desc: The same six points. All three bottom-left points are now filled circles and all three top-right points are triangles. Each centroid marker sits in the middle of its own group. The caption reads After iteration 2, 3 and 3, settled.

symbol.title: PCA draws new axes along the spread
symbol.desc: A long thin cloud of twelve points leaning up to the right. Two straight purple lines cross at the middle of the cloud: a long one along the cloud's length labelled PC1, the direction of most spread, and a short one across it labelled PC2, what is left over. One point has a short dashed line dropped onto the long axis, and the place it lands is ringed and labelled its PC1 value.
symbol.text: PCA: new axes, chosen by spread
PC1 — the direction of most spread
every point gets a PC1 value and a PC2 value

symbol.title: One sentence becomes one sparse row
symbol.desc: A box holding the sentence Great pizza, great service. An arrow labelled count leads to a row of eight narrow cells, one per vocabulary word, with the words written vertically above them. Five cells hold 0 in grey; the great cell holds 2 and the pizza and service cells hold 1, all outlined in pink. A note says five of eight cells are zero, so we store only the other three.
symbol.text: 5 of 8 cells are zero, so we store only the other 3
TF-IDF replaces each count with count × rarity

symbol.title: A shape error, with the offending line marked
symbol.desc: A console panel outlined in red shows a five-line Python traceback. The line that failed, Z1 equals X at W1, is highlighted and an arrow points at it from the right. The last two lines, printed in red, are a ValueError naming the two shapes 750 by 2 and 16 by 2 as not aligned.
symbol.text: Two shapes are printed. Compare them.

symbol.title: A terminal window frame
symbol.desc: A console window with a title bar reading Terminal. Inside, a prompt runs python hello.py, the output line reads hello, world, and a fresh prompt waits with a block cursor.

symbol.title: A traceback, with the offending line marked
symbol.desc: A console panel outlined in red shows a four-line Python traceback. The line that failed is highlighted and an arrow points at it from the right. The last line, a NameError, is printed in red.

symbol.title: Arrow pointing right
symbol.desc: A straight arrow pointing to the right.

symbol.title: Curved arrow
symbol.desc: A curved arrow that loops up and over to the right.

symbol.title: Correct badge
symbol.desc: A round badge with a tick inside, meaning correct.

symbol.title: Wrong badge
symbol.desc: A round badge with a cross inside, meaning wrong.

symbol.title: Labelled box
symbol.desc: A rounded box with a label inside.

symbol.title: Sticky note
symbol.desc: A sticky note with a folded corner and three lines of writing.

symbol.title: Data table
symbol.desc: A small data table with a shaded header row and six cells.

symbol.title: A DataFrame as a grid with a header row and an index
symbol.desc: A three-row table with a bold header row reading player, runs, over, a grey index column numbered 0 to 2, and the runs column outlined and tinted as the current selection.

symbol.title: A 2-D numpy array as a shaped block
symbol.desc: A block of three rows by four columns of numbers, with axis 0 arrowed downwards, axis 1 arrowed across, and the annotation shape 3 comma 4 below.

symbol.title: A train/test split as one cut of the deck
symbol.desc: A deck of 100 rows is cut by a dashed line into a train pile of 80 rows and a test pile of 20 rows.
symbol.text: one cut, then never mix them
